blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Earth rotates around an imaginary axis tilted at 23.5° from the vertical.
The 23.5° tilt is the single most important reason seasons exist on Earth.
Without an axial tilt, every location on Earth would receive nearly equal sunlight throughout the year, eliminating seasonal variation.
Earth's axis is tilted at 23.5° from the vertical (frequently asked value in geography exams).
Axial tilt—not distance from the Sun—is the primary cause of seasonal variation.
If Earth had no axial tilt, there would be no seasons due to equal sunlight distribution throughout the year.

blocks.content: If Earth had no tilt, every place would receive nearly equal sunlight throughout the year — resulting in no seasonal variation.
